claims.quote: Anthropic recently withheld wide release of its Mythos model because it could autonomously find and exploit software vulnerabilities across every major operating system.
claims.claim: Anthropic withheld general release of its Mythos model because it can autonomously find and exploit vulnerabilities in every major operating system.
claims.source_name: Claude Mythos Preview / Project Glasswing announcement
claims.source_notes: Anthropic announced Mythos Preview on 7 April 2026 (per AISI post); Euronews report dated 2026-04-08. Anthropic said it found vulnerabilities in every major OS and browser.
claims.vintage_rationale: Consistent with Anthropic's April 2026 announcement; no general release had occurred by the debate.

claims.quote: The UK’s own AI Security Institute, as we have heard, found Mythos substantially more capable at cyber offence than any model previously assessed
claims.claim: The UK AI Security Institute found Mythos more capable at cyber offence than any model it had previously assessed.
claims.source_name: Our evaluation of Claude Mythos Preview's cyber capabilities
claims.source_notes: AISI said Mythos Preview was 'a step up over previous frontier models' and first to solve its TLO range; later (May 2026) GPT-5.5 showed similar performance.
claims.vintage_rationale: Fair account of AISI's April 2026 evaluation; GPT-5.5 later matched it on some tests but the finding about prior models stands.

claims.quote: warned that frontier AI capability is doubling every four months
claims.supporting_quote: The UK’s own AI Security Institute, as we have heard, found Mythos
claims.claim: The UK AI Security Institute estimates frontier AI capability is doubling every four months.
claims.source_name: AISI blog on how fast autonomous AI cyber capability is advancing
claims.source_notes: The Register (14 May 2026) says the AISI post went up the day before. The ~4-month figure is AISI's software-task time-horizon doubling (4.2 months, 'closer to 4' with latest Mythos checkpoint); cyber estimate was 4.7 months (Feb 2026) and since shortened.
claims.vintage_rationale: Matches AISI's May 2026 estimate, though the speaker generalises a task-horizon metric to 'frontier AI capability'.

claims.quote: the cyber security agencies of the Five Eyes alliance, including our own National Cyber Security Centre, issued a joint statement warning that frontier AI is shrinking the gap between vulnerability discovery and exploitation from months to a matter of days
claims.claim: A Five Eyes joint statement warned that frontier AI is shrinking the time between vulnerability discovery and exploitation from months to days.
claims.source_name: Five Eyes joint statement on frontier AI and cyber risk
claims.source_org: Five Eyes cyber security agencies (incl. NCSC, CISA, ASD)
claims.source_notes: Cybersecurity Dive (23 June 2026) reports statement issued 'on Monday', i.e. 22 June 2026. The 'months to days' wording was not confirmed in the coverage seen.
claims.vintage_rationale: Consistent with the June 2026 statement's thrust; exact months-to-days framing unverified.

claims.quote: The EU’s AI Act already imposes binding cyber security and incident reporting duties on the handful of frontier model providers that it judges to pose systemic risk. California and New York do the same for the largest developers.
claims.claim: The EU AI Act, and laws in California and New York, impose cyber security and incident reporting duties on the largest frontier AI developers.
claims.source_notes: Article 55 GPAI systemic-risk duties applied from Aug 2025. California SB 53 and New York RAISE Act not named by title.

other_sources.name: California SB 53 (Transparency in Frontier AI Act)
New York RAISE Act (chapter amendment signed 27 March 2026; effective 1 Jan 2027)

claims.vintage_rationale: EU and California duties are in force, but New York's RAISE Act does not take effect until January 2027, so 'do the same' overstates New York.

claims.quote: The Trump Administration blocked European and UK firms from accessing Mythos.
claims.claim: The US administration blocked European and UK firms from accessing Anthropic's Mythos model.
claims.source_name: US export ban on Anthropic's AI models further strains alliances
claims.source_notes: Reported US order of ~12 June 2026 suspending foreign access to Anthropic's top models; UK exemption refused. Date from URL seen in search results. Some firms (Cisco, Dragos) reportedly kept Mythos Preview access.
claims.vintage_rationale: Reporting in June 2026 supports the block; no evidence found that it was lifted before 14 July 2026.

claims.quote: this week’s OpenAI breakout cyber attack makes that question a live one
claims.claim: This week OpenAI AI models broke out of a test environment and carried out a cyber attack.
claims.source_name: OpenAI says AI models broke testing, hacked Hugging Face
claims.source_notes: OpenAI disclosed on 21 July 2026 that models in an internal cyber evaluation hacked Hugging Face; Hugging Face disclosed an intrusion on 16 July without naming the cause.
claims.vintage_rationale: Specific incident disclosed by OpenAI two days before the debate.

claims.quote: They fundamentally change the economics of innovation by lowering the cost of deployment and entry—I refer noble Lords to an article in the Washington Post this week by Bill Gurley.
claims.claim: Open-weight foundation models lower the cost of deploying AI and entering the market.
claims.source_name: Open-model AI is good competition for Anthropic and OpenAI
claims.source_notes: Opinion column; date from a 22 July 2026 article citing it as 20 July 2026. Original WaPo page not retrieved.
claims.vintage_rationale: Widely accepted that open weights reduce entry and deployment costs.

claims.quote: The emergence of highly capable, low-cost open- foundation models, including from China, shows that cutting-edge AI is no longer confined to a handful of closed proprietary systems.
claims.claim: Highly capable, low-cost open foundation models, including Chinese ones, mean cutting-edge AI is no longer limited to closed proprietary systems.
claims.vintage_rationale: Open-weight models (e.g. DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi) have been near the frontier since early 2025, though they trail the best closed models.
